question.text: Fund SER (Cat III) has Series A1 units with Series Assets INR 27.04 crore, Series Liabilities INR 1.20 crore, Fund Expenses INR 32 lakh, and Management Fees + GST INR 45.74 lakh. 2,00,000 units are outstanding in Series A1. What is the Series A1 NAV per unit?

explanation.text: The Logic: Series Net Assets = 27,04,00,000 - 1,20,00,000 - 32,00,000 - 45,73,680 = INR 25,06,26,320. Series NAV per unit = 25,06,26,320 / 2,00,000 = INR 1,253.1316. This matches the Series NAV example on pp. 331-337. The Trap: INR 1,245.51 corresponds to a higher-fee series (e.g., A2/B1). INR 1,352 over-counts assets. INR 1,300 is a rough estimate without full deductions. Note: The workbook supports that the lower-fee A1 series has a higher NAV than higher-fee series, and that SEBI prohibits priority-distribution models in which one class subsidises another. Additional PPM-drafting guidance beyond that is not directly sourced in the cited pages.
